newsitem.title: GERMANY: German retailers hammer out another regional deal.
newsitem.headline: German retailers hammer out another regional deal.

text.p: German retail industry workers hammered out another regional wage agreement on Thursday, making it the third reached this year and raising hopes that a wave of strike action may now come to an end.
"We are done," Dirk Reimers, chief negotiator for the German white collar workers union in the Saar region said after five months of negotiations with employers.

The region's 43,000 shop workers will receive a 1.85 percent pay rise and a non-cash allowance for the planned extension of shopping hours. The deal was backdated to April 1 and will run for 12 months.

A similar deal was reached in Bavaria earlier this week and in the North-Rhine Westphalia region before that and now paves the way for the entire industry, comprised of nearly 3 million workers, to reach similar deals.

Retail industry wage talks were severely complicated when the German government agreed to overhaul antiquated and restrictive shop hour laws, allowing shops to stay open later during the week and on weekends from November.
Workers across Germany have staged periodic walkouts to demonstrate for better higher salaries and against longer shop hours throughout the summer.
